C0.quote: the task is to design a mechanism (or voting system)
C0.note: A jury of agents selects a collective winner through a sequential announcement (voting) mechanism; implementation-theoretic.

C1.quote: Mechanism 1 implements ϕ via backward induction
C1.note: Main results are a necessary condition and a mechanism for implementation via backward induction, i.e. properties of equilibria of the mechanism game.

C2.1.quote: outcome function mapping the agents' messages to a final winner

C2.2.note: The input is the announcement of a single candidate's name at each stage, or a choice between two candidates.

C2.3.quote: Each agent i has a preference function Ri
C2.3.note: Preference functions and the deserving winner are held by the agents independently of their messages.

C2.4.quote: g : M → N is an outcome function mapping the agents' messages
C2.4.note: Messages M_i are modelled separately from the preference functions R_i, and the paper discusses incentives to deceive.

C3.1.quote: new incentives to deceive emerge to prevent their enemy
C3.1.note: All analyses concern backward induction equilibria of strategic jurors.

C4.1.note: The input format is OTH (announcements); applicability condition not met.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: The objective is selecting the exogenous deserving winner (the 'socially optimal rule'), not welfare, efficiency, representation or distortion of voters.

VOT.quote_behav: each juror will strive to favor the candidate
VOT.quote_info: a finite sequential mechanism with perfect information implements
VOT.note: The deserving winner is explicitly known to all jurors. Knowledge of other jurors' preferences is only implied by the use of backward induction under perfect information. Jurors are also the candidates; they are coded here only, as jurors.

CAN.note: Candidates act only in their role as jurors, which is coded under VOT.

DES.quote_behav: the task is to design a mechanism (or voting system)
DES.quote_info: he does not know the actual functions
DES.note: The planner's objective (implementing the socially optimal rule) and its knowledge (the jury configuration and the admissible preference domain) are modelled explicitly.

C7.1.note: Both present types (jurors and planner) are goal-directed; no type is modelled as non-strategic.

C8.1.quote: the only outcome reached via backward induction is ωd
C8.1.note: Dominant strategies and Nash equilibrium are mentioned only in footnotes and related-work remarks, not as solution concepts of the main results.

C8.2.quote: implement the deserving winner via backward induction
